subject: URGENT: Nimbus Retail production errors & timeouts — possible SDK streaming/parser bug
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Nimbus Retail production errors & timeouts — possible SDK streaming/parser bug

Team —

Heads-up: Nimbus (account = Nimbus Retail, high-priority renewal next quarter) reports elevated 500s, higher-than-normal latency for streaming responses, and throughput collapse starting ~07:40 PST. They say several of their endpoints returned partial payloads and their consumer side then retried aggressively which caused additional load.

Key excerpt from customer: "clients saw a sudden spike in EOF-like parser failures during stream consumption; repeated reconnects and chunk reassembly failures." I've attached the error_log.txt they dropped in the ticket (attached).

Please triage urgently. Customer is escalating to their CTO and asking for an explanation and mitigation plan. Rafael, can you own the customer comms (I'll keep them looped). Dev/Hannah — please validate whether this is:
- a client SDK bug (JS/Node streaming parser or header handling)
- a server-side change that altered chunk framing or content-length behavior
- or a routing/buffering regression on our edge that could truncate streams

Ask: initial update to customer within 60 minutes, and a proposed mitigation within 3 hours. If we need leadership assistance for SLA/credits, ping Vivek.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: error_log.txt (text, 48KB)
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 09:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: Nimbus Retail production errors & timeouts — possible SDK streaming/parser bug

Marissa/Hannah —

I pulled the customer's logs. Quick observations:
- Multiple streams show chunks ending with truncated JSON fragments (closing braces missing) and repeated "Unexpected end of input" on the client.
- Upstream response headers in a few samples are missing Content-Length and are using Transfer-Encoding: chunked as expected, but the chunk boundaries look weird (a chunk size of 0 is occasionally duplicated).
- Our edge logs show a tiny spike in 502s around 07:39 that correlate with increased retries from the client IP range.

Hypothesis: a bug in our JS/Node client SDK streaming parser mis-handles back-to-back zero-length chunks when the connection is reset quickly, resulting in the client interpreting the stream as terminated early and retrying. That would explain the churn and throughput collapse. Another possibility is intermittent proxying behavior that duplicates the 0-sized chunk marker.

Immediate asks:
1) Can Hannah confirm whether our hosted runtime recently pushed any change to chunk framing/caching? (I checked deploys and see no model runtime changes after 03/08 but need infra logs.)
2) Rafael, please tell the customer we suspect a streaming parser interoperability issue and ask them to temporarily switch to our non-streaming (batch) endpoint for critical paths while we investigate. Provide exact curl example.
3) I'm going to create a lightweight toggle on the SDK to treat back-to-back zero-length chunks as no-op and not emit an early EOF. If that seems risky, we can ship a patch to their integration (CDN script) as a stop-gap.

I'll keep digging and post findings in INF-4721.

— Dev
Dev Patel | Senior SWE, Inference Runtime
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Jane Dalton <jane.dalton@nimbusretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 10:20:03 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: Nimbus Retail production errors & timeouts — possible SDK streaming/parser bug

Marissa / Rafael —

We are extremely frustrated. Our checkout/checkout-recommendations flow degraded starting 07:40 and we saw up to a 6x latency increase and ~18% 500 errors for streaming API calls. This impacted ~12% of live traffic and caused a measurable drop in conversions during the window.

We put a temporary band-aid in place (switched to batch endpoint for a fraction of traffic) but that has higher latency for users. We need:
- immediate mitigation to stop further customer impact
- a root cause and timeline to resolution
- confirmation of whether we should expect recurring incidents if we continue with the SDK patch

Our CTO is copied on the escalation and expects an update within 2 hours. Please advise now.

— Jane Dalton
Head of Platform Engineering, Nimbus Retail
jane.dalton@nimbusretail.com
Cc: support@nimbusretail.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 11:02:30 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: Nimbus Retail production errors & timeouts — possible SDK streaming/parser bug

Team —

Thanks for the rapid triage. Two quick directives to reduce customer impact and control optics:
1) Public-facing mitigation: Offer Nimbus an SLA credit pre-emptively (cover the impacted window) and propose a scheduled maintenance window to deploy a defensive change (either an SDK patch on their side or a small server-side tolerant parser) so they feel immediate action. Rafael, coordinate the credit language and get legal on standby.
2) Technical mitigation: Dev/Hannah — if the SDK toggle is low-risk, prioritize shipping a hotfix and provide a URL for a CDN-served patched client they can pull. Simultaneously enable a fallback route on our routing layer that sends Nimbus traffic to a pinned, non-optimized inference variant (slower but avoids the optimized chunking path) for 6 hours. That should restore throughput while we validate.
3) Postmortem: Run an RCA and include (a) request traces, (b) SDK version compatibility matrix, (c) mitigation timeline, (d) suggested long-term fix (parser robustness + better chunk validation and telemetry).

I'll join the call if needed. Also, loop DB/edge infra to see if any proxy upgrades or LBs changed config near the incident time.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | VP, GTM & Partnerships
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Dalton <jane.dalton@nimbusretail.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 07:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: Nimbus Retail production errors & timeouts — possible SDK streaming/parser bug

Jane —

Thank you for the quick mitigation on your side and for the logs — they were essential. Here is our coordinated update and immediate actions we've put in place overnight: 

What we did (last 12 hours):
- Rolled a hotfix toggle to the Node/JS SDK to ignore duplicated zero-length chunk markers (deployed to CDN and versioned as 2.1.7-hotfix).
- Enabled a routing fallback that pins Nimbus traffic to a compatible inference variant with conservative chunk framing for 6 hours starting 2026-03-10T00:30:00Z.
- Temporarily opened a hotline window for your engineering team; Rafael will coordinate the exact handoff.
- Applied a pre-emptive credit for the 07:40–08:10 PST window; Rafael, legal is following up with the formal note.

Next steps:
- Dev/Hannah to run stress tests on the patched SDK and validate no regressions in other customers' parsers by EOD.
- Postmortem (owner: Dev) with RCA and a plan to harden streaming telemetry and add chunk-integrity guards. Target date for postmortem: 2026-03-16.
- We'll provide a migration checklist for your integrators and a direct link to the patched CDN script.

Attachments: mitigation_playbook.pdf (playbook + rollback steps) and the log file you provided are in the ticket.

We appreciate the patience — we are treating this with executive priority. Rafael will follow up with the official SLA/credit paperwork.

Best,
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: mitigation_playbook.pdf (PDF, 210KB)
